question.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions to $\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-\frac{\pi }{4})=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ for $0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$

current_example.problem: Consider the equation $\sin\left(2x+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ for $-\pi < x \leq \pi.$ If the solutions $x_1,x_2,x_3,$ and $x_4$ are written in ascending order, what is the numerical value of $x_3\cdot x_4?$
current_example.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+\frac{\pi }{4} & =\frac{\pi }{4}+2n\pi , & \, & \, & 2x+\frac{\pi }{4} & =\frac{3\pi }{4}+2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x$ gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =2n\pi  & \, & \, & 2x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+2n\pi  \\ x & =n\pi  & \, & \, & x & =\frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi  \\  &  & \, & \, & x & =\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{4n\pi }{4} \\  &  & \, & \, & x & =\frac{(1+4n)\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm1,\pm2,\ldots$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $-\pi < x \leq \pi.$

- Setting $n=-1$ gives $x=-\pi$ and $x=-\dfrac{3\pi}4.$ We reject $x=-\pi$ since it lies outside the domain $-\pi < x \leq \pi.$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=0$ and $x=\dfrac{\pi}4.$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\pi$ and $x=\dfrac{5\pi}4.$ We reject $x=\dfrac{5\pi}4$ since it lies outside the domain $-\pi < x \leq \pi.$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $-\pi < x \leq \pi.$ So, the solutions $x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x_1 = -\dfrac{3\pi}4,\quad  x_2=0,\quad x_3= \dfrac{\pi}4,\quad x_4= \pi.
$$

Finally, we have

$$
x_3\cdot x_4 = \dfrac{\pi}{4} \cdot \pi = \dfrac{\pi^2}{4}.
$$
